review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on. `OrderedSimplexParams` is in OrderedSimplex.lean, and `paramValue`, `EdgeParam` and `paramsOfOrder` are in the Interpolation and Orders files. `unitCube` is defined as `Set.univ.pi fun _ => Set.Icc 0 1`. Mathlib has `Set.pi` and `Set.Icc` on Pi types, so the set can be expressed with existing operations. But `unitCube` is a thin, intentionally named specialisation over `F.EdgeParam`, and other files use it heavily (`isCompact_unitCube`, `measurableSet_unitCube`, `mem_unitCube_iff`). I found no duplicated API or repeated conversions that would justify replacing it. `orderedCubeSimplex` and `OrderedSimplexParams` express a chain `0 ≤ tₙ ≤ … ≤ t₁ ≤ top`. I found no Mathlib definition of a descending, bounded list with this bound structure (`stdSimplex` is a different concept). `cubeContribution` and `orderedCubeSectorContribution` are domain-specific integrals. The sort-based proof reuses `List.mergeSort`, so it does not duplicate Mathlib. I found no justified competing-concept finding. I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for a list-sortedness predicate matching `OrderedSimplexParams`.
